newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Feb natgas prices sink on weather, stocks-NGC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Feb natgas prices sink on weather, stocks-NGC.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices tumbled sharply in February, pressured by warmer U.S. weather patterns and adequate storage levels, Natural Gas Clearinghouse (NGC) said Friday.

U.S. spot gas prices for February averaged $2.78 per million British thermal units, down $1.18 from January's record of $3.96, which was the highest average price in the 11-year history of the NGC survey.
Prices into Columbia Gas tumbled $1 for the month to $2.85, still 50 cents over last year's levels, NGC said in its monthly survey.
Most Gulf pipes were off by about $1 for the month but were holding about 50 cents over year-ago levels.
The largest monthly losses were seen in Oklahoma, where Panhandle Eastern in Beaver County slumped by $1.45 to $2.75, still about $1 over the same year-ago month.
Sales into El Paso Natural Gas in west Texas averaged $2.65, down $1.40 for the month but still $1 above last year.

Prices represent NGC estimates of the median price for one month spot transactions at the indicated receipt points. The estimates are based upon quotes by industial end-users and local distribution companies, NGC said.
